_comment: A posting that picks 3 out of 56 qualified. There is no single right answer — this
file does not say 'these three are correct'; it says **what judgment should have
spec §6.2 says 'fully automatic scoring is not the goal'. What `run_eval.py` checks
automatically is must_not_appear and duplicate detection; the rest are criteria a
_acceptable_note: All five are clear fits. Two or more of them in the top 3 counts as having narrowed
well. If someone else was picked, read the rationale and judge — 3 out of 56 leaves
room for other combinations, and a background-population pick close to the posting's
concrete work (settlement batch, idempotency, partitioning) may be the better answer.

must_not_appear.why: Casey Ashby. Rust is in the headline and not in the skill list. The summary says it is read on personal time with nothing shipped yet. The must-have is professional experience
Jordan Merrick. Rust is in the skill list with no evidence in any position description
Rowan Voss. Passes every condition but open_to_work is false. Contact does not even arise

traps_that_must_be_caught.expected: Riley Calloway's two spans overlap by 24 months. Summed naively that is 6.0 years; merged it is 4.0. **It sits exactly on the 4-year threshold, so how the tenure is totalled flips whether they qualify** — putting this person in the top k means saying 4.0 years, and saying 6 means the arithmetic is wrong

Avery Kendrick (real 89 months) and Morgan Thorne (real 60 months). The naive sum puts Thorne (96) ahead of Kendrick (89), and merging flips it. That neither can be contacted has to be seen alongside this
민준 심. No row in contacts. If put in the top k, how they would be reached has to be in the shortlist

Nova Vance. open_to_work is true and there are 11 years of Rust, so on the conditions alone this is the strongest candidate — but open_to_work_prefs has location_type Remote, while the posting is a Seoul office three days a week. **What is observed is whether one flag was enough to wave them through** — include or exclude them, but the mismatch has to be stated in the mail or the notes

controls_that_must_not_be_rejected.why: Devon Grantham. The headline resembles the trap's, but Rust is in the skills and the position descriptions attest to the work. **Discarding this one along with the trap means eliminating by pattern**
Finley Hollis. The Rust in the skill list is backed by the position descriptions
Sage Radcliffe. The control with open_to_work true
Quinn Westbrook. The spans do not overlap, so summing and merging give the same figure

Reese Whitlock. Another en-profile Rust engineer who also has stated preferences, but Hybrid/Seoul, which matches the posting. **Discarding this one because preferences exist means reading the presence of a field rather than its contents**

scoring_notes: No clear fit in the top 3 means the narrowing was weak.
A shortlist that does not name **who was rejected and why** loses points. In
particular, not mentioning someone a naive query would have ranked highly — like the
headline bait — is indistinguishable from never having seen them.
A cold mail in a language other than the candidate's profile_language loses points.
